A view of the Ezhunnallathu (holy procession) ceremony as part of the Mannarasala Ayilyam festival
The call of Mannarasala Ayilyam awaits you. Visit Mannarasala Sree Nagaraja Temple from October 30 to November 2 to witness its time-honoured rituals, including the distinctive ritual of Rudra Ekadashini Kalashabhishekam, Mahadeepa kazhcha and the sacred observances of Pooyam Thozhal and Ayilyam day. Led by Mannarasala Amma, Divyashree Savitri Anthar- janam, the temple’s revered matriarch and chief priestess, the celebrations offer devotees an opportunity to experience a tradition preserved across generations and seek divine blessings.
Mannarasala Amma, Divyashree Savitri Antharjanam, arriving for darshan at Mannarasala Sree Nagaraja Temple as part of the Mannarasala Ayilyam festival
Mannarasala is revered as the abode of Lord Anantha and Lord Vasuki, the two divine serpent kings.The festivities here will begin on Friday, October 30, the auspicious day of Thiruvathira, with Ekadasha Rudrabhishekam to Lord Nagaraja, followed by Rudra Ekadashini Kalashabhishekam for Lord Mahadeva at 6.30 a.m. in a mandapam near the Illam’s Nilavara (cellar). The performance of a group of Thiruvathira will mark the start of the four-day celebrations.
The four-day Kalabha Muzhukappu for Lord Nagaraja and Queen Sarpayakshiyamma, which began on Rohini day (October 28), will conclude on October 31, On Punartham evening, second day of the Ayilyam festival, thousands of devotees will gather for the spectacular Maha Deepakazhcha.
Pooyam Thozhal will be held on Sunday, November 1, offering devotees an opportunity to seek the blessings of Lord Anantha. Amma will lead the Ucha Pooja. The observance will feature the ornamental image believed to embody Lord Anantha, who is believed to reside in the Nilavara. Following special poojas and offerings by Amma, devotees can have darshan of the deity.
At around 7 p.m., Amma and the younger female members of the Illam will visit the temple for darshan. The temple will close at 10 p.m.
The main observances will take place on Monday, November 2, beginning at 4 a.m. with Nirmalya Darshanam and Abhishekas. Special poojas will be led by the male family chief. The ornamental image of Lord Vasuki will adorn the main deity, Lord Nagaraja. Devotees can have darshan of Mannarasala Amma, Divyashree Savitri Antharjanam, near the Nilavara from 7.30 a.m. on Ayilyam day.
After the morning rituals, the family head will draw the Nagapadmakalam in front of the Nilavara. Amma will reach the temple after the kalam is completed. Following the customary ceremonies in the Sreekovil (sanctum sanctorum), the Ayilyam Ezhunnallathu, or holy procession, will begin around 1 p.m.
At the Illam, Amma will perform the Ayilyam Pooja, including the offerings of Noorum Palum and Guruthi. Later that night, Thattil Noorum Palum will be offered to Aakaasha Sarppangal (celestial serpents) by the family patriarch. Amma’s customary return to the temple for darshan will conclude the observances.
In keeping with temple customs, these special poojas and associated ceremonies are traditionally performed exclusively by the matriarchs of the Illam. If they are unable to conduct the rituals, it is customary for no one else to perform them. If the Ayilyam procession and poojas cannot take place as scheduled, the rituals will be conducted only within the temple under the leadership of the family patriarch. The festival will also feature cultural programmes selected to uphold the sanctity of the temple. The temple trust will present the Mannarasala Sree Nagaraja Awards to four distinguished artistes in dance, percussion, music and theatre, honouring their contributions and promoting traditional temple arts.

Guidelines for Devotees: Items required for making offerings (vazhipadu) related to Sarpadosha Pariharam are available at temple-run stalls at reasonable prices. Free parking facilities will be available at authorised parking areas under the temple. Devotees are advised to remain vigilant and avoid being misled by those deliberately creating traffic disruptions or overcharging for offering materials.
